# Feature: Mud tile — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #47 (Mud tile) from Terrain and Hazards before it is used in real levels. Effect: leaves footprints enemies can follow. Unique: terrain that stores your path for enemies to read. Useful: lay false trails, or avoid mud to stay untracked. Source status in the candidate file is 'trial'.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** leaves footprints enemies can follow.

**So that** lay false trails, or avoid mud to stay untracked.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Mud tile for the first time in its teaching room (mech-47-mud-tile-room). Teaching moment: First room: a muddy loop on the way to an orb, with a chaser in the level. A player who walks the direct muddy line leads the chaser along their own prints to the orb room and is caught there, which teaches that mud carries their route to enemies and that a false trail could have been left instead. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: You leave scent prints in mud
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: A chaser or patroller stepping into mud follows the order of your prints instead of its normal rule until the prints end
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Laying a loop of prints baits it in a circle

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.
- No soft-lock: every reachable state has a legal move, a lose, or a reset.
- Definition audit: mud: floor variant defined here; it stores the walked path as scent prints in walk order
- Definition audit: prints: record of the path walked per mechanic 45 in this file, with the explicit difference that enemies can read mud prints
- Definition audit: chaser: enemy that copies the player moves, per mechanic 32 in enemies-and-bots.yml; in mud it follows print order instead

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Mud tile's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Testing

Needs a mechanics playground: new — Test Level mech-47-mud-tile-room, built from this mechanic's teaching moment above. What to check there: every rule in Player-Facing Behavior, played in mech-47-mud-tile-room; the teaching moment's first (naive) action should fail as described and the corrected action should succeed. Record play sessions for replay: yes — sessions are the review evidence. Synergy rooms are explicitly deferred to a later run and are not part of this feature's check.
Named test cases (from the candidate file; all must be played):
- Test case prints record order: walking a bent path in mud stores the prints in walk order, readable start to finish
- Test case enemy follows prints: blocked-by: 32 (chaser): an enemy entering the mud follows the print order instead of its normal rule until the prints end
- Test case adversarial false trail: blocked-by: 32: a loop of prints baits the enemy around the loop while the player exits by a dry route; avoiding mud leaves no trail at all
- Test case restart and replay: restart clears every print, and a recorded session replays to the same end state
